chapter: Fats Waller, Zululand and the ideal band
title: Fifty years as a professional; Slam Stewart and Tatum
summary: He marks fifty years playing and recalls Cleveland with Tatum and Slam.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: I'm very proud really of what, of it really when I think of it. Like I've been playing professionally since I was sixteen years old. And I'll be 66 next March. So I've been playing professionally for 50 years. So I'm going to give myself a gold star right in the center of the forehead. (LAUGHTER).
You will have to join that, be invited to join that Golden Monocle Club of the Johnny Walker Society.

Now I think that's really quite marvellous and I haven't heard Slam Stewart, I suppose I'm revealing something of my own age now, but I haven't been in Washington for over twenty years. I left there in 1950 so that's certainly twenty years ago. It's been about twenty five years since I've heard Slam Stewart.

You were missing something because he just gets better and better. And I know that besides, he worked with me last, oh when the heck was it, May or June or something like that up there in Syracuse. But the last time we played together was with Art Tatum out in Cleveland, Ohio. Slam Stewart was on bass and I've got a lovely picture of that too by the way, that you should have. We had it taken.

Marian was there as well.
Art Tatum, he was crazy about Marian. He thought,
oh he thought she was a killer.
Well she is. (LAUGHTER). She is, yes.
He liked her playing and liked her as a person too.
